title: Innocent Rouge
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Sequel to Innocent, loosely based on the real Sanson family, hereditary executioners of Paris. On the eve of the French Revolution, Charles-Henri Sanson carries out royal executions while his sister Marie-Josephe, who shaves her head and dresses as a man, claims a role at the scaffold and pursues power and freedom in a brutal, decadent society. The story follows the family into the Revolution and the guillotine era.
life_message: The story asks whether anyone can stay innocent in a cruel system, and celebrates defiance of the roles society assigns.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Family honor and personal vengeance (Alain's killing) drive action.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Marie-Josephe defies every rule of sex and rank.

Civic vs kin.evidence: The Sanson family line shapes every choice.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Aristocratic hierarchy is shown as rotten and challenged.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Church and crown are depicted as hollow.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival in a brutal era meets fierce self-expression.

folkways.japan: A Japanese reimagining of French history; the theme of inherited family occupation (ie) and its burdens resonates with Japanese family-role norms.

delivery.evidence: ANN guide reviewers (Friedman, Lemus) call it nuanced and do not call it preachy; Friedman finds each awful character relatable.

personified.ideology: defiance of assigned gender and social roles

delivery.note: The politics are carried by the Sanson family's choices, and reviewers describe aristocrats and rebels alike with detail rather than caricature.

winners_losers: Marie-Josephe's defiance is celebrated; the aristocracy and the old order lose. Sympathy goes to rebels against assigned roles.
